'''Hannes Steinbach''' (born 1 May 2006) is a German [[basketball]] player for the [[Charlotte Hornets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-16 |title=Husky Hoops Signs German Big Man Hannes Steinbach |url=https://gohuskies.com/news/2025/4/16/mens-basketball-husky-hoops-signs-german-big-man-hannes-steinbach.aspx |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=University of Washington Athletics}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=HANNES STEINBACH {{!}} Adidas Next Generation Tournament |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/ngt/players/hannes-steinbach/012867/ |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=Euroleague Basketball}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
The son of former Würzburg Bundesliga player Burkhard Steinbach, he went through the Würzburg Baskets youth program,<ref>{{Cite web |last=AG |first=iWelt |date=2024-07-31 |title=ERSTER PROFIVERTRAG FÜR YOUNGSTER HANNES STEINBACH |url=https://www.wuerzburg-baskets.de/news/newsdetails/erster-profivertrag-fuer-youngster-hannes-steinbach |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=www.wuerzburg-baskets.de |language=de}}</ref> and was also coached by his father for a time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-06 |title=Sein Vater ist Würzburger Basketball-Legende: Wie Hannes Steinbach die großen Fußstapfen noch größer machen will |url=https://www.mainpost.de/sport/wuerzburg/sein-vater-ist-wuerzburger-basketball-legende-wie-hannes-steinbach-die-grossen-fussstapfen-noch-groesser-machen-will-art-11379750 |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=mainpost |language=de}}</ref> With the Würzburg men's second team, he was promoted to the [[ProB|2nd Bundesliga ProB]] in 2024 as champions of the 1st Regionalliga Süd-Ost (South-East Regional League).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-27 |title="Farmteam" steigt in die 2. Liga auf |url=https://www.fnweb.de/sport/vereine_artikel,-wuerzburg-baskets-farmteam-steigt-in-die-2-liga-auf-_arid,2190322.html |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=www.fnweb.de |language=de}}</ref> In the summer of 2024, Steinbach signed his first professional contract with [[Würzburg Baskets|Würzburg]], and he made his debut in the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] at the end of September 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hannes Steinbach: Alle Infos & Statistiken |url=https://www.easycredit-bbl.de/spieler/56613 |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=www.easycredit-bbl.de}}</ref>

In April 2025, Steinbach announced his decision to move to the United States for the [[2025–26 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2025–26 season]], to attend the [[University of Washington]], following the path of other well-known Germans ([[Detlef Schrempf]], [[Chris Welp|Christian Welp]], and [[Patrick Femerling]]).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-03 |title=Back to a Reliable Source, Huskies Add German Player |url=https://www.si.com/college/washington/recruiting/back-to-a-reliable-source-huskies-add-german-player-01jqy3r2gctq |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=Washington Huskies On SI}}</ref> In the 2024–25 Bundesliga main round, Steinbach averaged 7.2 points and 5.8 rebounds in 31 appearances. In the subsequent ten games of the quarter-final and semi-final series for the German championship, he increased his averages to 14.8 points and 10.4 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hannes Steinbach: Alle Infos & Statistiken |url=https://www.easycredit-bbl.de/spieler/56613 |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=www.easycredit-bbl.de}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman, Steinbach averaged 18.5 points and 11.8 rebounds per game while shooting over 57% from the field. He was named to the third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] and the Big Ten All-Freshman Team. Steinbach declared for the [[2026 NBA draft]] following the season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sevilla |first1=Lucien |title=Hannes Steinbach declares for 2026 NBA Draft |url=https://www.dailyuw.com/article/hannes-steinbach-declares-for-2026-nba-draft-20260416 |website=The Daily |access-date=April 20, 2026 |date=April 16, 2026}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
On June 23, 2026, Steinbach was selected with the fourteenth overall pick by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the [[2026 NBA draft|2026 NBA Draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=sportschau.de |title=NBA-Draft: Zwei deutsche Talente schaffen Sprung in die NBA |url=https://www.sportschau.de/basketball/nba/nba-draft-steinbach-anderson,nba-draft-steinbach-anderson-100.html |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=sportschau.de |language=de}}</ref>

==National team career==
Steinbach was selected to represent Germany for the first time at the youth level in [[2023 FIBA U18 European Championship|2023]], where he helped the [[Germany men's national under-18 basketball team|Germany U18 national team]] win bronze.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farkas |first=Katalina |date=2024-08-13 |title=EM-Titel für U18-Basketballer: Hannes Steinbach und Ivan Kharchenkov im Porträt |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/sport/u18-basketball-europameister-dbb-lux.MbNN4Dccjb9Y6tJHRZLP9s |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=Süddeutsche.de |language=de}}</ref> In April 2024, he helped the U18 team win bronze at the [[DBB Albert Schweitzer Tournament|Albert Schweitzer Tournament]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-07 |title=U18-Nationalspieler Hannes Steinbach lässt bei internationalem Basketballturnier aufhorchen |url=https://www.main-echo.de/sport/weitere/hannes-steinbach-auf-den-spuren-von-papa-art-8208595 |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=www.main-echo.de |language=de}}</ref> A few months later, Steinbach was dominant at the [[2024 FIBA U18 EuroBasket]], helping Germany win their first title at the U18 level, averaging 15.4 points and 12.7 rebounds per game, while also being named to the tournament's All-Star Five.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farkas |first=Katalina |date=2024-08-13 |title=EM-Titel für U18-Basketballer: Hannes Steinbach und Ivan Kharchenkov im Porträt |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/sport/u18-basketball-europameister-dbb-lux.MbNN4Dccjb9Y6tJHRZLP9s |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=Süddeutsche.de |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|date=8 August 2024|title=Hannes Steinbach 2024 FIBA U18 EuroBasket profile|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-u18-eurobasket-2024/teams/germany/339855-hannes-steinbach|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=20 September 2025}}</ref>

In July 2025, Steinbach helped Germany reach the final of the [[2025 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2025 FIBA U19 World Cup]], where they lost to the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-06 |title=U19-Basketballer verpassen Sensation im WM-Finale |url=https://www.sport1.de/news/basketball/wm/2025/07/u19-basketballer-verpassen-sensation-im-wm-finale |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=SPORT1 |language=de}}</ref> Throughout the competition, Steinbach was the best German player in several statistical categories at the U19 World Cup, averaging 17.4 points and 13 rebounds per game, while earning a spot on the tournament's All-Star Five.<ref>{{cite news|date=6 July 2025|title=USA's AJ Dybantsa named TISSOT Most Valuable Player|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-u19-basketball-world-cup-2025/news/usas-aj-dybantsa-named-tissot-most-valuable-player|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=9 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|date=6 July 2025|title=Hannes Steinbach 2025 FIBA U19 World Cup profile|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-u19-basketball-world-cup-2025/teams/germany/339855-hannes-steinbach|work=fiba.basketball|access-date=20 September 2025}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Steinbach's father Burkhard is a retired basketball player who played with [[Dirk Nowitzki]] during his time at [[DJK Würzburg]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA - "Kenne dich seit deiner Geburt": Dirk Nowitzki mit emotionaler Botschaft an Hannes Steinbach |url=https://www.basketball-world.news/artikel/kenne-dich-seit-deiner-geburt-nowitzki-mit-emotionaler-botschaft-an-steinbach-1230783 |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=basketball-world |language=de-DE}}</ref>
